difficultyReason: Clear paradox with one obvious confounding variable. A town's park attendance fell despite expansion; a new entertainment complex opened nearby. Only one answer addresses both horns: competing attraction.
stimulus: The Riverside Park was expanded by 40 percent last year, adding new trails and recreational facilities. Yet the total number of park visitors declined by 15 percent. Curiously, surveys show most residents still view the park favorably.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The park's survey asked only residents who lived within one mile of the park.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A new indoor recreation complex opened nearby during the same year and charges lower admission than the park.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The park's expansion project created temporary disruptions that lasted several months.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Residents who use the park consider it one of the town's most important community assets.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The park's maintenance budget did not increase proportionally with the expansion.

explanations.correct: If a competing attraction (cheaper rec complex) opened the same year, it explains why attendance fell despite the park's expansion. The park improved, but visitors migrated to a cheaper alternative. Both facts are now consistent.
explanations.A: Survey methodology doesn't explain the actual decline in visitor numbers.
explanations.C: Temporary disruptions might explain a short-term dip, but the question implies a sustained decline.
explanations.D: Favorable views don't resolve why actual attendance dropped.
explanations.E: Maintenance budget doesn't address the core paradox of expanded facilities yet fewer visitors.

difficultyReason: Straightforward paradox: expensive drug reduces treatment costs overall. One obvious confound: drug prevents a much costlier downstream condition. Only answer addressing both halves.
stimulus: A new pharmaceutical treatment costs three times as much as the standard therapy for early-stage hypertension. Yet hospitals that adopted the new treatment reported a 20 percent decrease in their overall treatment costs for hypertensive patients within two years.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new treatment is covered by most major insurance plans.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients taking the new treatment are more likely to adhere to their medication regimen.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The new treatment reduces the incidence of stroke and heart attack, which are far more expensive to treat than hypertension itself.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hospitals began tracking treatment costs more carefully after adopting the new treatment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The standard therapy has been in use for over thirty years.

explanations.correct: If the new treatment prevents much more expensive complications (stroke, heart attack), it saves money downstream despite its upfront cost. This reconciles the high per-patient cost with lower overall costs.
explanations.A: Insurance coverage doesn't explain why hospitals' overall costs decreased.
explanations.B: Adherence alone doesn't explain the cost savings without addressing what the drug prevents.
explanations.D: Accounting practices don't create actual cost savings.
explanations.E: Age of the standard therapy is irrelevant to the cost paradox.

difficultyReason: Clear two-part discrepancy: book sales up, but bookstore locations down. One obvious resolution: online retail diverted traffic. Direct confounding variable.
stimulus: Over the last decade, book sales in the United States increased by 12 percent. However, the number of independent bookstores declined by 30 percent during the same period.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Large bookstore chains have also experienced a decline in the number of their retail locations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The average price of books has increased over the last decade.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Online retailers and digital formats have captured a growing share of the book market.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Many independent bookstore owners have retired and not been replaced.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Readers are purchasing books from a wider variety of genres than they did ten years ago.

explanations.correct: If online retailers and digital formats have grown, they explain how total book sales can increase while brick-and-mortar locations decline. Books are still selling; the channel has shifted.
explanations.A: Chain decline doesn't resolve the discrepancy; it deepens it.
explanations.B: Price increases might explain some sales growth, but don't address store closures.
explanations.D: Retirement of owners is a causal factor in closures, but doesn't explain why total sales rose.
explanations.E: Genre diversity doesn't relate to the sales-vs.-locations paradox.

difficultyReason: Simple paradox: test scores up, student satisfaction down. One clear confound: test difficulty increased, so higher scores reflect harder test, not better teaching.
stimulus: In recent years, students' standardized test scores at Lincoln High School have risen steadily, yet student satisfaction surveys indicate that academic morale is at its lowest point in a decade.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The school hired several new teachers with advanced degrees in their respective subjects.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The standardized test was redesigned to be significantly more difficult, and the scoring scale was adjusted upward accordingly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Student satisfaction surveys were administered online, which may have increased response rates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The school increased the frequency of standardized testing from twice a year to three times a year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Many of the school's most experienced teachers retired during this period.

explanations.correct: If the test became harder and the scale adjusted upward, higher scores don't reflect improved student learning—they reflect a measurement artifact. Students may feel stressed by harder material, explaining lower satisfaction.
explanations.A: New credentialed teachers should improve satisfaction, contradicting the data.
explanations.C: Survey administration method doesn't address the content paradox.
explanations.D: More frequent testing might explain lower satisfaction, but not the score rise directly.
explanations.E: Teacher retirements should lower scores, not raise them.

difficultyReason: Straightforward paradox: restaurant hours reduced, but profit increased. One obvious resolution: reduction eliminated unprofitable late-night hours. Single confounding factor.
stimulus: A downtown restaurant recently reduced its operating hours by closing late-night service. Yet the owner reports that monthly profits have increased since the change was implemented.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The restaurant had been using the same suppliers for over five years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The late-night customers typically ordered less food than daytime customers and tipped smaller amounts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The restaurant is located in an area with high pedestrian traffic during the day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other restaurants in the area remain open late at night.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The owner reduced prices on breakfast items after eliminating late-night service.

explanations.correct: If late-night customers spent less and tipped less, eliminating those hours removes unprofitable business. Profits rise despite fewer operating hours. Both facts are reconciled.
explanations.A: Supplier relationships don't explain the profit paradox.
explanations.C: Daytime traffic is good, but doesn't explain why profits rose when hours decreased.
explanations.D: Competitor hours don't affect this restaurant's profit paradox.
explanations.E: Price reductions would lower profits, not raise them.

difficultyReason: Clear paradox: forest area stable, but biodiversity declining. One obvious confound: remaining forest is fragmented and degraded. Environmental science example with single clear resolution.
stimulus: According to recent surveys, the total forest area in the region has remained relatively constant over the past fifteen years. Yet the number of native bird species inhabiting those forests has declined by 25 percent.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Some migratory bird species have altered their migration patterns in response to climate change.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The remaining forests have been fragmented into smaller, isolated patches due to development, reducing habitat quality for many native species.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Local hunting regulations were relaxed during the same period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: New forest management policies have increased the harvesting of deadwood, which was previously left on the forest floor.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The surveys were conducted using different methodologies in the early and late periods.

explanations.correct: If forests are fragmented into isolated patches, the total area may be constant but habitat quality and connectivity decline, explaining the loss of bird species despite stable forest acreage.
explanations.A: Climate-driven migration changes don't explain habitat loss in a stable forest.
explanations.C: Relaxed hunting might further harm populations, but doesn't explain species loss in stable forests.
explanations.D: Deadwood harvesting is a management detail; doesn't address the quantity-vs.-quality paradox.
explanations.E: Methodological differences don't explain real ecological decline.

difficultyReason: Simple paradox: museum admission free, but operating costs up. One obvious resolution: free admission increased volume, raising facility and staffing costs. Direct causal link.
stimulus: The Riverside Museum eliminated its admission fee last year to increase attendance. The museum did indeed see a 35 percent increase in visitors. However, the museum's annual operating costs increased by 40 percent.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain this apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The museum did not adjust its staff levels when the admission fee was eliminated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Many of the museum's visitors are residents of the surrounding neighborhood.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cost of maintaining the museum's exhibits has not changed significantly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Free admission required increased custodial, utility, and security resources to accommodate more visitors.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The museum conducted a survey before eliminating the admission fee.

explanations.correct: If higher visitor volume requires more custodial, utility, and security resources, costs rise despite the loss of admission revenue. This explains why visitor numbers up by 35% but costs up by 40%.
explanations.A: Fixed staffing doesn't explain the cost increase beyond visitor volume.
explanations.B: Neighborhood composition doesn't explain the cost paradox.
explanations.C: If maintenance costs unchanged, other operational costs (utilities, custodial, security) must have risen.
explanations.E: Pre-policy surveys don't address the actual cost paradox.

difficultyReason: Clear paradox: country exports more, trade deficit grows. One obvious confound: imports grew even faster. Simple arithmetic-based discrepancy with one clear resolution.
stimulus: The country's exports increased by 8 percent last year, yet the overall trade deficit grew to its highest level in a decade.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exchange rates have become more stable in recent years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The country's imports increased by 15 percent during the same period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The country's largest trading partners also increased their exports to other nations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Government trade policies were relatively unchanged during the past year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Consumer confidence in the country increased significantly last year.

explanations.correct: If imports grew 15% while exports only grew 8%, the deficit gap widens. Both facts are consistent: exports up but imports up faster, net negative gap grows.
explanations.A: Exchange rate stability doesn't explain the trade deficit growth.
explanations.C: Other nations' exports don't directly affect this country's trade balance.
explanations.D: Policy consistency doesn't address the paradox.
explanations.E: Consumer confidence might affect imports, but doesn't directly resolve the discrepancy.

difficultyReason: Straightforward paradox: technology investment high, worker productivity unchanged. One obvious resolution: transition period and retraining costs offset immediate gains. Clear temporal confound.
stimulus: Apex Manufacturing invested heavily in new automation technology last year, yet measurements of worker productivity per hour showed no significant improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The company's competitors have not yet adopted similar automation technology.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Workers required extensive retraining and the company experienced startup inefficiencies during the first year of implementation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The new technology was purchased from an international supplier.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The company's profit margins decreased slightly during the same period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Worker satisfaction surveys showed improved morale after the technology was installed.

explanations.correct: If retraining and startup inefficiencies offset the technology's gains in the first year, productivity shows no net improvement despite the investment. Gains should materialize later.
explanations.A: Competitor status doesn't affect this company's productivity paradox.
explanations.C: Supplier location is irrelevant to productivity outcomes.
explanations.D: Profit margins don't directly explain worker productivity stagnation.
explanations.E: Worker morale doesn't resolve why measured productivity didn't improve.

difficultyReason: Simple paradox: popular law yet enforcement rare. One obvious resolution: law is symbolic/political, with low enforcement resources. Clear discrepancy between adoption and implementation.
stimulus: A city council unanimously passed a new environmental ordinance that was hailed as groundbreaking by environmental advocates. Yet city officials report that the ordinance is almost never enforced due to resource constraints.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The city council consists of eight members, all of whom support environmental protection.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Environmental ordinances in neighboring cities have also faced enforcement challenges.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The environmental ordinance contained detailed requirements that are expensive to monitor and enforce.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Advocates plan to challenge the ordinance in court if it is strictly enforced.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The city has experienced budget cuts in recent years.

explanations.correct: If the ordinance is expensive to monitor and enforce, the city council could unanimously support it (politically popular) while enforcement remains impractical (resource-intensive). Both facts coexist.
explanations.A: Council support doesn't explain why enforcement is lacking.
explanations.B: Other cities' challenges don't explain this city's specific paradox.
explanations.D: Legal challenges don't explain current non-enforcement.
explanations.E: While budget cuts might enable the paradox, they don't explain why the council passed an unenforceable law, or define the relationship between passage and enforcement.
